title: A path integral is little arrows joined head to tail
text: In the QED lectures he draws each amplitude as a little arrow. Arrows for indistinguishable paths are added head to tail; the probability is the square of the length of the sum.

support.source: QED: The Strange Theory of Light and Matter

title: Calculus is zooming in and slicing, not a formula sheet
text: A derivative is what you see when you zoom in until a curve looks straight. An integral is a sum of thin slices. The formula sheet is a record of those two ideas, not a substitute for them.

title: Notation is a cane, not a leg
text: In high school he found the textbook's trig notation easy to misread, so he made up his own symbols and only translated back at the end.

title: Erasing one bit costs a little heat
text: In the lectures on computation he follows a plain question: why a computer gets hot. Erasing a bit is not free. Landauer's limit says forgetting one bit costs at least kT ln 2 of heat.

title: To simulate nature, build a machine that follows nature's rules
text: A classical computer that stores every amplitude of a quantum system runs out of room very fast. His 1982 argument is to simulate the quantum system with a machine that obeys the same quantum rules.

title: There is plenty of room at the bottom
text: In 1959 he asked why we could not write the Encyclopaedia Britannica on the head of a pin, and then go on down to arranging atoms one by one.
aliases: plenty of room at the bottom

support.source: There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom, December 29, 1959

title: A license plate miracle is a target drawn afterwards
text: A license plate that looks miraculous is usually a target drawn after you saw it. If you do not say in advance which plate would count, the surprise is fake.

title: Mental cube roots run on approximation, not brute force
text: In Brazil he raced an abacus seller to the cube root of 1729.03. He worked by approximation and by knowing nearby cubes, not by grinding out every digit.
